subject: Using residuals from one part of a hierarchical model in another

messages.author: 326c11520dc1d655
messages.subject: Using residuals from one part of a hierarchical model in another
parts:
Hello!

I am trying to put together a hierarchical model with two parts - the first is a von Bertalanffy growth model run in jags. People sometimes use the residuals from the von Bertalanffy curve as an index of growth rate, but the model to make the curve/index is run separately from the model used to find out what is explaining variation in the index.  

Because this information all comes from one data set, I am hoping to be able to combine those steps, and use the residuals of the first part as a response in the second part of the model.

The first part should be (I think) like this:

size ~ dnorm(mu, tau)
mu <- von Bertalanffy equation 
residual <- size-mu

Right now, because it can't define residual twice, I have the second part of the model as:

X ~ dnorm(mu1, tau1)
mu1 <- beta*residual + alpha

X represents a variable that might have a relationship with residual. That runs, but I don't think that is doing what we want, and it should be more like:

residual ~ dnorm(mu1,tau1)
mu1 <- beta*X + alpha

The objective is to find out whether X is explaining variation in residual, using residual as an index of growth rate.

So,  my two questions are (1) is calculating and using residuals this way appropriate/allowed in a Bayesian hierarchical model? And (2) if that is ok to do, is it possible to define the residuals in a way that would allow them to be used as a response rather than a predictor while keeping it in the same model as X, instead of two different models?

I'd super appreciate any thoughts folks have. Thank you for taking the time to read this!

Sarah
